plan.summary: A standard 12-month view of Microsoft built only from primary filings and as-of market data, organised around the operator's three questions. (1) Cloud margin durability: read FY2026 10-K property-and-equipment, lease and capitalised-software disclosures against FY2025 and FY2024, plus the FY2026 Forms 10-Q for intra-year estimate changes, capex run-rate and leases commencing mid-year. (2) The multiple: a reverse DCF from filed cash flows and 2026-09-24 market data, solved across a stated discount-rate range rather than one modelled point, with share-based compensation treated as a cost and every input given a named provider and retrieval date. (3) AI revenue: decompose revenue by product and service and by segment FY2023-FY2026 only after each line's comparability across any recast is confirmed, under a bounding method fixed before the section runs, and declare the question unanswerable from primary disclosure if no bound is traceable. No figure appears in this plan; every number in the report comes from stored facts and recorded calculations. The prior research supplied with this request shapes which questions are asked and is not cited as evidence.

challenges.statement: The four-year trend base and the whole AI-growth decomposition assume that segment definitions and the 'revenue by product and service' categories are comparable across FY2023-FY2026. The plan names no risk that presentation was recast or reallocated between those years, and prescribes no method for handling non-comparable lines. If categories were re-cut, growth_outlook and historical_financial_analysis would produce differences that are presentational rather than economic, and nothing in the plan would catch it.
challenges.suggestion: Add a first step in segment_analysis: check each 10-K for recast/reclassification language and confirm whether FY2023 and FY2024 figures were restated. Record the comparability status of every line before any growth attribution, and mark non-comparable lines as such rather than differencing them.

challenges.statement: valuation_dcf and scenarios_sensitivities depend on a cost of capital, and the only market input planned is the 10-year Treasury yield. No source is named for the equity risk premium, beta or cost of debt, yet cost of equity is an explicit sensitivity axis. Without a named, recorded provider for those inputs, the reverse DCF's discount rate has no traceable origin and the sensitivity grid has no defensible centre point.
challenges.suggestion: Name a provider and retrieval date for each remaining discount-rate input (ERP, beta or an alternative equity-cost method, marginal cost of debt from the filed debt note, effective tax rate), or state that the reverse DCF will be run across a stated discount-rate range instead of a point estimate.

challenges.statement: Share-based compensation is absent from every section focus. It bears directly on all three operator questions: it is a non-cash add-back inflating the operating-cash-flow-to-FCF bridge that cash_flow_analysis builds, it affects the diluted share count feeding the reverse DCF, and capital_allocation's buyback-versus-reinvestment framing cannot be read without knowing how much repurchase merely offsets dilution.
challenges.suggestion: Add SBC and its cash-flow and dilution effects to cash_flow_analysis and capital_allocation, sourced from the cash flow statement and equity/SBC note, and state whether the reverse DCF treats SBC as a cost.

challenges.statement: No FY2026 Forms 10-Q are planned, only annual reports plus two transcripts. A change in estimated useful life, a step-change in quarterly capex, or leases commencing mid-year appear first in the quarterly filings, and the annual report may disclose only the full-year effect. The catalysts section also promises scheduled FY2027 earnings dates and meeting dates, for which no source is listed at all.
challenges.suggestion: Add MSFT's FY2026 Forms 10-Q as a source for intra-year depreciation, capex run-rate and any estimate change disclosed mid-year, and name the company IR events page (or the proxy) as the source for scheduled dates used in catalysts.

challenges.statement: growth_outlook proposes to attribute FY2026 growth to lines 'that did not exist or were immaterial three years ago', but the filed product-and-service categories are long-standing buckets; AI revenue would sit inside existing lines rather than forming new ones. The stated fallbacks, RPO and deferred revenue, are equally undifferentiated by product. The section may therefore consume its budget and return a non-answer without having defined what a bound would even look like.
challenges.suggestion: Before running the section, define the bounding method and the criterion for declaring the question unanswerable: e.g. whether MD&A attributes growth-rate points to AI services, whether any new line appears, and what upper bound RPO duration can support. State the fallback answer form explicitly.

challenges.statement: Twelve sections, seventeen sources, a reverse DCF and a multi-axis sensitivity grid is a heavy load for standard mode, and the plan sets no priority. Peripheral work (a five-year capital allocation record, proxy incentive metrics, peer useful-life benchmarking) competes for the same budget as earnings_quality and valuation_dcf, which carry two of the three operator questions.
challenges.suggestion: State an explicit ordering: earnings_quality, valuation_dcf and growth_outlook resourced first, with capital_allocation, proxy and peer benchmarking marked as trimmable if evidence gathering on the PP&E, lease and useful-life disclosures runs long.

critique.coverage_note: The plan is unusually disciplined on evidentiary status, prior-research handling and prompt-injection, and its named risks are honest about what filings cannot answer. My challenges are gaps rather than misdirection: comparability of restated segment lines, unnamed discount-rate inputs, missing SBC and 10-Q coverage, an under-specified AI-bounding method, and no prioritisation. I take no view on the company or on the plan's likely conclusions.

sections.focus: Step one, before any differencing: read the FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 10-K segment and revenue notes for recast, reclassification or reallocation language and record whether FY2023 and FY2024 figures were restated onto the current basis. Label every segment and product-and-service line comparable, restated-comparable or non-comparable; no growth attribution is permitted on non-comparable lines. Then capture segment revenue and operating income FY2024-FY2026, identify which lines carry cloud and AI revenue, and record where cost-of-revenue and depreciation allocation across segments is disclosed.

Question one. Test whether reported margin expansion is supported by cash economics or by capitalisation: changes in estimated useful lives of server and network equipment across FY2024-FY2026 and any disclosed earnings effect, including estimate changes first disclosed in an FY2026 10-Q; construction in progress not yet depreciating; finance versus operating lease classification and leases commenced mid-year; capitalised internal-use software and its amortisation; equity-method and other-income items tied to investees. Compare D&A growth with gross PP&E growth. Mark any policy disclosed without a sized effect as unsized.

Four-year trend base FY2023-FY2026 from the FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 10-Ks: revenue, gross and operating margin, depreciation and amortisation, capital expenditure and returns on invested capital, all computed by the calculation layer. Build series only on lines the segment_analysis comparability check marked comparable or restated-comparable; present non-comparable lines as separate stubs, never as one continuous series. Supplies the denominator for the AI-growth work and the base rates against which the reverse DCF is tested.

Reconcile operating cash flow to net income and to free cash flow after additions to property and equipment and finance lease principal payments. Separate share-based compensation as a non-cash add-back and show free cash flow both before and after treating it as an economic cost, since it is the largest discretionary item in that bridge. Track the capex-versus-depreciation gap, working capital including receivables and deferred revenue, and whether the build is funded from operations, debt issuance or balance-sheet assets. Use the FY2026 10-Qs for the quarterly capex path.

Question three, under a method fixed in advance. Test in order: (a) whether any product-and-service or segment line appears in FY2024-FY2026 that was absent in FY2023; (b) whether MD&A or the earnings release attributes growth-rate points to AI services; (c) whether the remaining performance obligation disclosure gives an amount and duration that can cap AI-attributable contracted revenue. If none yields a bound traceable to filed data, the stated answer is that AI revenue is not separable from primary disclosure, naming what would have to be disclosed. Management commentary is recorded as assertion only.

Question two as a reverse DCF. Take market capitalisation and enterprise value implied by price and share count as of 2026-09-24, and have the calculation layer solve for the revenue growth, operating margin and reinvestment path consistent with that value. Run it across a stated discount-rate range rather than one point, with each input recorded by provider and retrieval date: risk-free rate, published equity risk premium and beta, marginal cost of debt from the filed debt note, effective tax rate from the tax note. Treat share-based compensation as a cost and say so. Present conditions, not a fair value.

Sensitivity of implied value to the variables question one identifies: useful-life and depreciation schedule, capital expenditure intensity, cloud operating margin, terminal growth and discount rate. The discount-rate axis is centred on the range used in valuation_dcf, not on a single modelled point. Include a scenario in which capacity enters service faster than contracted revenue absorbs it, and one in which the disclosed remaining performance obligation converts on schedule. All grid values produced by the calculation layer.

Five-year record of capital expenditure, finance lease commitments, acquisitions, strategic investments, dividends and repurchases from the cash flow statements and equity notes. Read buybacks against share-based compensation and the diluted share count roll-forward, distinguishing repurchase that merely offsets dilution from repurchase that shrinks the share base. Assess whether reinvestment intensity has displaced shareholder returns and whether buyback pace changed as the build accelerated. Include disclosed purchase and construction obligations as forward claims on cash.

Assemble the thesis from the verified findings above, stated as conditions with their evidence: what the filings show about margin composition, what the reverse DCF requires across the discount-rate range, and what remains unmeasurable from primary disclosure. Separate the supported core from the judgement layer explicitly, and carry forward the comparability labels so no conclusion rests on a differenced non-comparable line.

Risks grounded in this run's evidence: fixed depreciation and lease charges against uncontracted demand, concentration the filings do not disaggregate, antitrust and cloud-licensing remedies, AI model liability and emerging AI regulation, goodwill and intangible carrying values. Size each from disclosure where a number exists and mark the rest unsized. Re-test independently whether risks named in prior research are still present in the FY2026 filings and 10-Qs; do not carry any of them over on prior authority.

Dated events inside the 12-month horizon, each with a named source: scheduled FY2027 quarterly earnings dates and the annual meeting date from the company investor relations events page and the DEF 14A; the Q1 FY2027 10-Q that will first show the post-FY2026 depreciation run-rate; proxy voting items; and any regulatory decision dates named in legal proceedings or subsequent-event disclosures. State for each which of the three operator questions its disclosure would resolve.

Written last, from validated sections only, with no figure that is not a stored fact and no growth comparison drawn across a line marked non-comparable.

themes.label: Enterprise cloud migration and infrastructure spend
themes.rationale: Azure is Microsoft's largest growth engine, riding continued enterprise workload migration off-premises; growth rate and consumption trends are a core driver of the equity story.

themes.label: Generative AI product monetization
themes.rationale: Copilot attach rates across Microsoft 365, GitHub and Azure represent the company's primary bet on converting AI investment into incremental per-seat and consumption revenue.

themes.label: Grid electrification and power constraints
themes.rationale: Data center power availability increasingly gates Microsoft's ability to bring AI capacity online, linking its growth pace to utility interconnection and grid buildout timelines.

assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Regressed against S&P 500 on monthly total returns to 2026-09-24, over 72 paired observations. The proxy and the window are both judgements and both change the answer, which is why this is a proposal rather than an input.

assumptions.name: capex_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of capital expenditure over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1205, 0.1326, 0.1814, 0.2291, 0.3494.

assumptions.name: depreciation_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of depreciation and amortisation over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.0736, 0.0637, 0.0816, 0.0994, 0.1175.

assumptions.name: ebit_margin
assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.4206, 0.4177, 0.4464, 0.4562, 0.4678.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Derived EBITDA margin is ~52.9% (EBIT 44.2% + D&A 8.7%), but capex intensity ran 12.1% to 34.9% of revenue over FY22-FY26 and finance-lease interest tripled, so EBITDA overstates cash far more than it did for the old licence-led Microsoft. At ~8-9% WACC and 3% growth, Gordon-consistent EV/EBITDA is roughly 9-12x on current capex, ~15x+ only if capex fades toward D&A. 14x splits that against mature megacap software comps trading high-teens. I regard the perpetual-growth estimate as the better terminal value here, because the multiple route silently imports today's AI-era pricing. Raise toward 18x if capex normalises; cut to 10x if it does not.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2022-06-30 to 2026-06-30, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 198,270,000,000 to 331,839,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 4.96% on 2026-09-22, as published by 2026-09-24 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.0496.

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.justification: The mean of income tax expense over pre tax income across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1311, 0.1898, 0.1823, 0.1763, 0.1940.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a WACC of at least ~8% (risk-free 4.96% per the derived fact, plus an equity premium on a sub-1 beta), so the Gordon denominator stays wide. 3% sits above long-run US nominal GDP-ish inflation-plus-a-little, which I justify by the category mix: productivity software, cloud infrastructure and advertising are growing share of GDP and MSFT has pricing power. It is not the 13.7% trailing CAGR, which reflects an AI capex cycle that cannot persist perpetually. Lower to 2.0-2.5% if you think cloud pricing commoditises; 3.5% only if you accept perpetual share gain.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.
